statement: Compute the J2-induced nodal regression rate of a circular Earth orbit at 400 km altitude with 51.6 degree inclination. Use J2 = 1.08263e-3. Answer in rad/s (sign matters: westward drift for prograde orbits is negative).

oracle_cards.name: j2-nodal-regression

variables.Omega_dot: rate of change of the right ascension of the ascending node [rad/s]
variables.J2: second zonal harmonic of the primary [dimensionless]; J2 = 1.08263e-3 for Earth
variables.p: semi-latus rectum [m]; p = a(1 - e^2). For circular orbits, p = a

oracle_cards.when: Earth-orbiting satellite, secular J2 perturbation. Negative for prograde (i<90°), positive for retrograde. (Hintz §5.4)

oracle_cards.name: mean-motion
oracle_cards.when: Two-body orbit.

canonical_method: a = R_earth + h;  for circular orbit p = a, e = 0
Omega_dot = -(3/2) * J2 * (R_earth/p)^2 * n * cos(i), i in radians

statement: Compute the inclination required for a sun-synchronous circular Earth orbit at 800 km altitude. (Sun-sync means the orbit plane precesses with the Earth's motion around the Sun, so Omega_dot = 2*pi / sidereal_year.) Use J2 = 1.08263e-3 and sidereal year = 31 558 149.5 s. Answer in radians.

oracle_cards.name: j2-nodal-regression
oracle_cards.when: Earth-orbiting satellite. (Hintz §5.4)

oracle_cards.name: sun-synchronous-condition
oracle_cards.when: Sun-sync: orbit-plane precession matches Earth's mean motion around the Sun (so local solar time at ascending node is preserved).

oracle_cards.name: invert-for-inclination
oracle_cards.when: Sun-sync orbits are always slightly retrograde (i > 90°), so cos(i) is negative.

statement: A spacecraft is on a Hohmann transfer from a 400 km circular Earth orbit to GEO (35 786 km altitude). At the transfer apogee, you simultaneously circularize AND rotate the orbital plane by 28.5 degrees in a single combined impulsive burn. Compute the magnitude of that single burn in m/s.

oracle_cards.name: combined-maneuver-law-of-cosines
oracle_cards.equation: delta_v = sqrt(v_t^2 + v_c^2 - 2 * v_t * v_c * cos(theta))

variables.v_t: transfer-ellipse speed at the maneuver point [m/s]
variables.v_c: target circular speed at the same radius [m/s]

oracle_cards.when: Combine a plane change with an in-plane speed change in one burn. ALWAYS cheaper than doing them separately. (Hintz §3.6)

oracle_cards.name: vis-viva
oracle_cards.when: Any point on a Keplerian orbit.

oracle_cards.name: circular-orbit-speed
oracle_cards.when: Circular orbit.

canonical_method: delta_v = sqrt(v_t^2 + v_c^2 - 2 v_t v_c cos(theta)), theta in radians

statement: A satellite is in an orbit with eccentricity 0.2 and is currently at a true anomaly of 120 degrees. Compute the corresponding mean anomaly M (in radians) using Kepler's equation. (The eccentric anomaly E is an intermediate step.)

oracle_cards.name: eccentric-anomaly-from-true
oracle_cards.equation: tan(E/2) = sqrt((1-e)/(1+e)) * tan(nu/2)   ⇒   E = 2 * atan(sqrt((1-e)/(1+e)) * tan(nu/2))
oracle_cards.when: Elliptical orbit. (Hintz §2.4)

oracle_cards.name: kepler-equation
oracle_cards.when: Kepler's transcendental equation, elliptical orbit. (Hintz §2.4)

statement: Compute the heliocentric orbital period of Mars using Kepler's third law. Use Mars's semi-major axis = 2.279 392 × 10^11 m and mu_sun = 1.327 124 × 10^20 m^3/s^2. Answer in seconds.

oracle_cards.name: kepler-third-law
oracle_cards.when: Two-body orbit. CRITICAL: use mu of the central body — mu_sun for heliocentric orbits, NOT mu_earth.

statement: Compute the synodic period of Earth and Mars (the time between successive Earth–Mars launch opportunities). Use Earth's sidereal year = 31 558 149.5 s. oracle_cards.when: Two bodies orbiting the same primary; the synodic period is the time between successive identical relative configurations. (Hintz §3.5)

oracle_cards.name: kepler-third-law
oracle_cards.when: Two-body orbit.

Compute the total delta-v of the MORE EFFICIENT (lower delta-v) of the two options. Sum the magnitudes of all burns in the chosen transfer.

oracle_cards.name: circular-orbit-speed
oracle_cards.when: Circular orbit.

oracle_cards.name: vis-viva
oracle_cards.when: Any point on a Keplerian orbit.

oracle_cards.name: hohmann-total-dv
oracle_cards.when: Direct Hohmann between two coplanar circular orbits.

oracle_cards.name: bi-elliptic-total-dv

variables.v_t1p: vis-viva at r_1 on first ellipse
variables.v_t1a: vis-viva at r_b on first ellipse (apogee)
variables.v_t2a: vis-viva at r_b on second ellipse (apogee)
variables.v_t2p: vis-viva at r_2 on second ellipse (perigee)

oracle_cards.when: Bi-elliptic via intermediate apogee r_b > r_2. Three impulsive burns.

oracle_cards.name: choose-the-smaller
oracle_cards.when: When two valid options are compared, the more efficient one is the smaller delta-v.

canonical_method: Compute delta_v_h via Hohmann (a_t = (r_1+r_2)/2, vis-viva twice).
Compute delta_v_be via bi-elliptic (a_t1, a_t2, vis-viva four times).

statement: A spacecraft is on a hyperbolic Earth-encounter trajectory with hyperbolic excess velocity v_infinity = 5 km/s. At closest approach (periapsis), its speed is 12 km/s. Compute its periapsis radius in meters.

oracle_cards.name: hyperbolic-energy-equation
oracle_cards.when: Any point on a hyperbolic (or parabolic, with v_infinity = 0) trajectory. Energy conservation: specific kinetic energy = v_infinity^2/2 + mu/r is constant. CRITICAL: speeds in (m/s)^2 NOT (km/s)^2 — convert before squaring.

oracle_cards.name: solve-for-r-periapsis
oracle_cards.when: Algebraic rearrangement of the energy equation at periapsis.

canonical_method: Convert v_p and v_infinity to m/s if given in km/s.

statement: A satellite is in orbit around Earth with an orbital period of 7200 s. Using Earth's gravitational parameter mu = 3.986004418e14 m^3/s^2, compute the orbit's semi-major axis in meters.

oracle_cards.name: semi-major-axis-from-period
oracle_cards.when: Invert Kepler's third law T = 2*pi*sqrt(a^3/mu) by solving for a.

statement: A spacecraft orbits Earth on an elliptical orbit with semi-major axis a = 8.0e6 m. At the instant it is at radial distance r = 7.0e6 m from Earth's center, compute its speed in m/s. Use mu = 3.986004418e14 m^3/s^2.

oracle_cards.name: orbital-speed-from-energy
oracle_cards.when: Solve the energy equation v^2/2 - mu/r = -mu/(2a) for v (the vis-viva relation).
